verified_against_binary: v2.36.4 makes the contract page's own promise true. That page says 'Each rule links to the page that explains it'; it did not. Every list item did contain an <a>, which is why a naive count said 52/52 -- but the link was the TIER BADGE pointing at the on-page legend. The only navigation to an explanation was the section heading, so a reader met 52 bold one-liners with nothing to click through to. Each rule is now a link to its own explanation: HTML deep-links to a per-fact anchor, Markdown links to the explaining page (markdown has no stable fragment ids). Anchors are derived from the FACT ID, never the rule text -- ten rules were reworded across v2.36.1-3, and a prose-derived anchor would break every inbound link on each rewrite. The build's existing fragment gate validates all 52 deep links; three tests pin the count parity across both formats, the anchor resolution, and the id-not-prose derivation. No fact changes.
note: Design note: the contract page is deliberately NOT expandable. Its stated contract is 'generated from the rules on every other page, with no additional prose ... this page cannot disagree with the others'. Inlining details would duplicate the whole site and reintroduce exactly the drift the page exists to rule out. Linking is the fix; expanding is not.
